config.trigger: The frozen baseline reported 93.1% interval coverage at a true +4 pp effect, with its 95% Wilson Monte Carlo interval below nominal 95%.
config.secondary_effects_interpretation: Descriptive calibration checks only; no confirmatory claims across the full grid.
config.primary_interval: Two-sided Welch household difference-in-means 95% interval, unchanged from baseline.
config.monte_carlo_interval: 95% Wilson interval for the proportion of repetitions whose target interval contains the known effect.

decision_rule.upper_below_0.95: Follow-up provides evidence of undercoverage at +4 pp; preserve the estimator and investigate a separately preregistered method study.
decision_rule.lower_above_0.95: Follow-up provides evidence of overcoverage at +4 pp; investigate a separately preregistered method study.
decision_rule.otherwise: Monte Carlo interval includes nominal coverage; this is inconclusive, not proof of calibration.

prohibited_changes: Do not reuse the baseline seed.
Do not change the DGP, sample size, effect grid, estimator, interval, or primary effect after observing follow-up results.
Do not modify the frozen baseline report or analysis plan.

interpretation: Monte Carlo interval includes nominal coverage; this is inconclusive, not proof of calibration.

calibration_flags: At true effect 0 pp, the Monte Carlo coverage interval excludes nominal 95% coverage. Investigate in a new, prospectively specified simulation study; do not tune this run to pass.
At true effect 10 pp, the Monte Carlo coverage interval excludes nominal 95% coverage. Investigate in a new, prospectively specified simulation study; do not tune this run to pass.
results.scope: Target inference only, using the same household return DGP. Null rejection is false-positive rate; non-null rejection is two-sided power. Wilson intervals quantify Monte Carlo uncertainty. Candidate-surrogacy certification is not implied.

review_status: Self-review only; no independent peer review has occurred.
